description:
`fz_bitstring_is_binary` is declared in RUNTIME_SYMBOLS, the provenance
authority, and was absent from the ~115 hand-written `builder.symbol` calls that
tell the JIT where things live. On macOS the JIT falls back to dlsym over the
process image and finds the no_mangle export anyway; a Linux executable does not
export its symbols to dlsym, so there the same program died:

    thread 'main' panicked at cranelift-jit/src/backend.rs:243:
    can't resolve symbol fz_bitstring_is_binary

    matrix::to_string::run                  FAILED
    matrix::to_string_bitstring_panics::run FAILED

The six-target local gate was green throughout and could not have been anything
else: the hole is invisible on the platform it is checked on.

FIXED (9a13dbbef). RUNTIME_SYMBOLS was made the single provenance authority in
fz-5xp.3 and that list was a second copy of the same fact that had already
drifted, so the set became a TABLE, `runtime_symbol_addrs`, which can be read
back and checked.

WHAT 'BY CONSTRUCTION' TURNED OUT TO MEAN. The filing said the registration
should be DERIVED from the authority so a declared symbol is registered by
construction. It cannot be: an address table has to exist somewhere, because
only Rust can take `ir_runtime::fz_x as *const u8`, and RUNTIME_SYMBOLS lives in
the fz crate and carries the ABI rather than addresses. The honest guarantee is
a TEST, and the test has to allow the second legitimate way a declared symbol is
reachable -- native codegen lowering the call in place and never asking for an
address. That is the arithmetic shims, whose five near-identical `matches!` arms
in prim.rs collapsed into one `ARITH_SHIMS` table so the escape hatch is a
nameable set rather than a claim; a second test refuses any entry in it that fz
does not declare.

`every_declared_runtime_symbol_is_reachable_from_compiled_code` fails with
exactly ["fz_bitstring_is_binary"] when the registration is removed again.

Same shape as fz-5xp.59: a symbol that resolves on the development platform by
accident.
title: The JIT's symbol table is a second, hand-maintained copy of RUNTIME_SYMBOLS, and it is already missing one
